findings: NVIDIA_API_KEY is read only from the environment (secrets.require_api_key) and the workflow supplies it only via ${{ secrets.NVIDIA_API_KEY }} on the single evaluation step; no echo, set -x, or workflow-level exposure. Workflow permissions are contents: read.

All subprocess output and HTTP bodies pass through secrets.redact before being written (live._run, live._http, smoke, results, pipeline failure reasons, compose logs). Redaction is exact-match only, so transformed or partial key forms would not be caught; accepted as low risk since no code path transforms the key.

The key-bearing Compose .env is written with mode 0600 outside the evidence directory, and S1 refuses an upstream dir inside the run dir, so the uploaded artifact and committed evidence cannot contain it. A grep of the repo found no real nvapi- keys. The only match is the fake test key nvapi-TESTONLY-k3y in tests.

Postgres password and AUTH_SECRET are generated per run with the secrets module, not hardcoded. The upstream clone is pinned to commit cdaf61e and verified after checkout. The fixture mount is read-only and contains synthetic data only.

The workflow_dispatch inputs run_dir and configuration are interpolated into a shell run line. Only repo writers can dispatch, and configuration is a choice, but run_dir is free text, so a low-severity shell injection is possible with write access. Recommend passing it through an env var (RUN_DIR) in a follow-up. Not blocking.

Plain-HTTP calls go only to localhost for the local stack. The key is sent as a Bearer token only to the hosted NIM endpoints. The MCP check runs in-process, so no network endpoint is exposed and no unauthenticated service is opened.
